story._note: The recruit card story (Backstory.story, v0.014; Douglas: 'more of a story, less of a list'). ONE short story in time order, built only from recorded facts: where he comes from (family, land or none, town), then up to four beats from his own life history (jobs, service, idle spells, wounds) and the family's events (debts, land and house lost, wages unpaid, hunger, kin's deaths) and the town's (sacked, famine), joined by cause where the record supports it (no field -> hired work; a loss -> the next job or service), then why he stands before the captain (his family's real hardship), with his temper and his ambition (and a like, where it fits his work) woven in. Clauses carry no dates: the code adds them ('in the autumn of year 1', 'that winter', 'since ...'). Placeholders: {full} his full name, {first}, {subj} him (pronoun or first name, chosen by the code), {pro} he/she, {pos} his/her, {fam}, {fams} plural, {famw} the culture's word for a family, {town}, {head}, {land}, {lv} / {lvs} the land verb (plural / singular), {what} 'a tanner's hand at the Thorne tanner', {crop}, {force}, {span}, {a0}-{a2} the event's arguments, {rel} 'Gerd's brother', {how}, {weeks}, {debt_c} '30 coins', {winters}, {a_town} 'an Oakford', {lead} temper + hardship, {pay}, {amb} / {amb_ing} ambition, {weapons}, {drink}. 'cultures' override any key per town culture (middle, northern, eastern, orc, goblin, moon_elf, dwarf).
